mainTopic: Learning a man's forbidden relatives from his wife's, and the source for his daughter from a woman he raped.
overview: The amud opens by testing whether a man's own relatives (הוא) can be learned from his wife's relatives (היא). The גמרא knocks the comparison down in several ways, using the two views on whether סקילה or שריפה is the harsher death. רבא then shows that the ban on his wife's daughter-in-law cannot be learned from his own daughter-in-law under either method of comparison: דון מינה ומינה or דון מינה ואוקי באתרה. Next, the גמרא asks for the source that a man's daughter from a woman he raped is forbidden. It brings three answers: אביי's קל וחומר, רבא's double גזירה שוה, and the teaching of אבוה דרבי אבין from ובת איש כהן. It then looks for the matching אזהרה, and רבי אילעא brings 'אל תחלל את בתך להזנותה'. That פסוק leads to teachings about a father who marries his daughter to an old man or delays the marriage of his grown daughter. The amud ends as אביי begins to explain רבי עקיבא's saying about who is truly 'poor'. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Her side is more severe because her mother gets burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning his relatives from hers. On her side the mother is punished with שריפה, which is more severe than his mother's punishment of סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about her relatives? They are special because one who is with her mother gets burning. Can you then say the same about his relatives, where one who is with his mother gets stoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the idea of learning the man's relatives from his wife's relatives. It points out that the two sides are not equal in severity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn one case from another if the two are truly alike. On the wife's side, being with her mother (his חמות) is punished with שריפה. On his side, being with his own mother is punished with סקילה. According to the view that שריפה is more severe, the wife's side is stricter, so it cannot teach about his side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about X, since it has...': a formula for rejecting a comparison by showing that X has something special

steps.confusionAlert: This objection only works if you hold that שריפה is more severe than סקילה. Step 3 shows what happens under the opposite view.

phrases.english: What about her relatives?
phrases.notes: 'Her' means the man's wife, so these are his wife's relatives.

phrases.english: they are special, since her mother is punished by burning;
will you say the same about his relatives,
where his mother is punished by stoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed comparison of הוא to היא (from before this section) by showing a difference in severity.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempt to learn the man's relatives from his wife's relatives.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source (her side) is more severe, since her mother gets שריפה, than the target (his side), since his mother gets סקילה.

steps.title: Her side punishes all the same, his side does not
steps.stepSummary: A second objection: on her side, her daughter and her mother's mother get the same punishment. On his side, his daughter and his mother's mother do not. So the two sides do not match.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, if 'he' is like 'she': just as for her you made no difference between her daughter and her mother's mother, so too for him you should make no difference between his daughter and his mother's mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why the comparison fails. If the sides really matched, his relatives would all get one punishment, the way hers do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the wife's side, both her daughter and her mother's mother are punished with שריפה. On his side, his daughter gets שריפה but his mother's mother gets סקילה. Since his side splits into two punishments and her side doesn't, the two sides are not truly parallel.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And furthermore': brings in an additional objection
'You did not make a difference': treated the same

phrases.english: And furthermore, if he is like she:
just as with her you did not make a difference
between her daughter and her mother's mother,
so too with him, you should not make a difference
between his daughter and his mother's mother.
phrases.notes: But in fact his daughter gets burning and his mother's mother gets stoning, so the match breaks down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate objection to the same comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison of הוא to היא as a whole.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Her side has one uniform punishment, but his side has two different punishments, so the parallel is incomplete.

steps.title: Even for the view that stoning is more severe, the comparison fails
steps.stepSummary: For the view that סקילה is the more severe death, the first objection does not work. But the other objection is still enough to block the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says stoning is more severe, it cannot be learned because of this difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes sure the rejection works for every opinion. It tells us which objection still blocks the comparison for someone who holds סקילה is more severe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 depended on שריפה being more severe. If סקילה is more severe, his side would actually be stricter, and that objection falls away. Even so, the difficulty that the two sides don't match still stops the comparison, so it fails under both views.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to the one who says': applying the point to a particular opinion
'We derive it': learn it through comparison

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison of 'his relatives' to 'her relatives' fails under both views of which death is more severe. For one view it fails because of severity, and for the other because the two sides don't line up.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says stoning is more severe,
because of this difficulty, we cannot derive it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sorts out which of the previous objections works for the opposing view on severity.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under either view of severity, his relatives cannot be learned from hers by this comparison.

steps.title: Then her daughter-in-law should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: Another challenge to the comparison: if the two sides are equal, then just as his daughter-in-law is forbidden, her daughter-in-law should also be forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as on his side his daughter-in-law is forbidden, so too on her side her daughter-in-law should be forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more problem with treating his side and her side as equal. The comparison would lead to a result we don't accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the comparison runs the other way, from his side to hers. His כלה (his son's wife) is forbidden to him. If the sides truly matched, his wife's כלה (her son's wife) would also have to be forbidden to him, which the question treats as a surprising result.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': introduces a problem that follows from the idea

phrases.english: If so: just as with him, his daughter-in-law is forbidden,
so too with her, her daughter-in-law should be forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another challenge to the הוא כהיא comparison, this time showing a result that would follow if the comparison were reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that his relatives and her relatives are fully parallel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Full parallelism would mean her daughter-in-law is forbidden to him just like his own daughter-in-law, and the question presents that as a result we don't accept.

steps.title: אביי: The Verse Limits It to Your Own Son's Wife
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the challenge from the פסוק 'אשת בנך היא': a man is liable only for his own son's wife, not for his wife's son's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The verse says, 'She is your son's wife.' You make him liable because of your son's wife. You do not make him liable because of her son's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from Step 4 by pointing to a word in the פסוק that limits the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have just said 'your daughter-in-law.' Instead it adds 'she is your son's wife,' stressing your own son. אביי reads this as excluding the wife of your wife's son, so the comparison does not reach her daughter-in-law.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says; the גמרא is bringing a proof from a פסוק
Her son's wife (the wife of his wife's son)

phrases.english: Abaye said: the verse says:
"She is your son's wife."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:15

phrases.english: Because of your son's wife you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת בְּנָהּ.
phrases.english: but you do not make him liable because of her son's wife.
phrases.notes: 'Her son' here means his wife's son, and 'her son's wife' is that son's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since his relatives and her relatives are compared, her daughter-in-law would be forbidden like his
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'אשת בנך היא' limit liability to his own son's wife

steps.title: רבא: Under Either Method of Comparison, It Does Not Follow
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a different answer: whichever method of comparison you use, the prohibition of her daughter-in-law cannot be derived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whether you follow the one who says 'learn from it, and from it,' or the one who says 'learn from it, and put it in its own place,' this law does not come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to Step 4. He says the comparison fails no matter which method is used, and he will explain each one next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to learn one case from another. In דון מינה ומינה, everything carries over, including the punishment. In דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, you learn the basic law but keep the details of the new case. רבא claims that neither way produces the prohibition, so אביי's פסוק is not needed for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and from it: take the law and its details from the source case
Learn from it, but set it in its place: take the law, but keep the details of the new case
It does not come out; it cannot be derived

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whether according to the one who says "learn from it, and from it,"
phrases.notes: Meaning: when you learn one case from another, you take over all its details too.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְאַתְרַהּ״
phrases.english: or according to the one who says "learn from it, and set it in its own place"
phrases.notes: Meaning: you learn the basic law, but the details follow the new case's own rules.

phrases.english: – it does not come out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: The method of comparison itself fails
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison would extend the prohibition of a daughter-in-law to her side
steps.terutzMaskana: Under both methods of comparison, the prohibition is not derived

steps.title: What Full Comparison Would Teach: Prohibition and Stoning
steps.stepSummary: Under דון מינה ומינה, the comparison would teach two things: her daughter-in-law is forbidden, and the punishment is סקילה, just like for his daughter-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'learn from it, and from it': just as on his side his daughter-in-law is forbidden, so too on her side her daughter-in-law is forbidden. And from it again: just as on his side it is by stoning, so too on her side it is by stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא lays out what the comparison would teach under the first method. This sets up the next step, where he shows that this comparison can be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under דון מינה ומינה, you cannot take only the prohibition. The full detail comes along too, so her daughter-in-law would carry סקילה, like his daughter-in-law. That full package is what רבא will attack next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He' / 'she': shorthand for his relatives and her relatives
Stoning, one of the four death penalties of בית דין

phrases.english: According to the one who says: learn from it, and from it,
just as for him – his daughter-in-law is forbidden,
so too for her – her daughter-in-law is forbidden.
And from it: just as for him it is by stoning,
so too for her it is also by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רבא's claim
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under דון מינה ומינה, the comparison would make her daughter-in-law forbidden with the punishment of סקילה

steps.title: The Comparison Is Refuted: His Mother Gets Stoning, Hers Only Burning
steps.stepSummary: For the view that סקילה is more severe, the full comparison can be refuted. His side is stricter, because his mother is punished with סקילה while her mother gets only שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says stoning is more severe, there is room to refute: What about his side? His mother is punished by stoning. Will you say the same about her side, where her mother is punished by burning?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows that, under the full-comparison method, the comparison can be knocked down, at least for the view that סקילה is the harsher death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot learn a harsh punishment (סקילה) for her side from his side if his side is shown to be stricter. His mother carries סקילה, the harsher death on this view, while her mother carries only שריפה. So his side cannot teach סקילה for her daughter-in-law.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute; the comparison can be knocked down
Burning, one of the four death penalties

steps.confusionAlert: This refutation uses the same mother-versus-mother point as Step 1. But here רבא uses it to block the full comparison, which would carry סקילה along with it.

phrases.english: According to the one who says: stoning is more severe,
there is room to refute:
What about his side? His mother is punished by stoning.
Will you say the same about her side, where her mother is punished by burning?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: סְקִילָה חֲמוּרָה, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the full comparison laid out in Step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The דון מינה ומינה comparison, for the view that סקילה is more severe
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His side is stricter (his mother gets סקילה, hers only שריפה), so it cannot teach סקילה for her side

steps.title: A second objection: her daughter burned but her daughter-in-law stoned?
steps.stepSummary: Under the full comparison, her daughter-in-law would get stoning while her own daughter gets burning. That seems backwards.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: her daughter is punished with burning, and her daughter-in-law would be punished with stoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another reason to reject the full comparison of step 7. It finds it strange that a more distant relative would get a harsher death than a closer one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sleeping with his wife's daughter is punished with שריפה. If her daughter-in-law got סקילה, which this line treats as harsher, the more distant relative would carry the heavier death. That looks illogical, so the comparison seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. It brings in an extra objection.
Her daughter, meaning his wife's daughter.
Her daughter-in-law, meaning his wife's son's wife.

phrases.english: And furthermore: her daughter is by burning
phrases.notes: "Her" means his wife. Sleeping with his wife's daughter is punished with burning.

phrases.english: and her daughter-in-law by stoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the full comparison, next to the one in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full comparison (דון מינה ומינה) giving her daughter-in-law סקילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A closer relative (her daughter) gets the lighter death, so a more distant one (her daughter-in-law) should not get the harsher one.

steps.title: His own relatives prove that this pattern can happen
steps.stepSummary: The objection fails, because on his own side his daughter gets burning and his daughter-in-law gets stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He himself proves it: his daughter is punished with burning, and his daughter-in-law with stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the objection of step 9. The very same 'strange' pattern already exists in the Torah for his own relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With his own relatives, his daughter (closer) gets שריפה and his daughter-in-law (more distant) gets סקילה. So a distant relative getting the harsher death is not illogical at all. The objection of step 9 is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: He himself will prove it. His own case shows the objection is wrong.
His daughter-in-law, meaning his son's wife.

phrases.english: He himself will prove it,
phrases.notes: "He" means the man's own relatives. The same pattern already shows up there.

phrases.english: for his daughter is by burning
and his daughter-in-law by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection raised in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the objection of step 9, not the whole problem with the comparison.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The objection assumes a distant relative cannot be punished more harshly than a close one, but his own daughter and daughter-in-law show it can.

steps.title: The real problem: her daughter-in-law should match her mother
steps.stepSummary: On his side, his mother and daughter-in-law get the same punishment. So on her side, her daughter-in-law should match her mother and get burning. That clashes with the full comparison, which gives stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: just as with him, you did not make a difference between his mother and his daughter-in-law, so too with her, you should not make a difference between her mother and her daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason the full comparison fails. Copying his pattern exactly leads to a result that contradicts itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On his side, his mother and his daughter-in-law both get סקילה. If we copy that pattern, her daughter-in-law should get the same as her mother, which is שריפה. But the full comparison (step 7) said her daughter-in-law gets סקילה. The two results clash, so the full comparison breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings in the real explanation after the rejected one.
You did not distinguish, meaning you gave them the same law.

phrases.english: Rather: just as he —
you did not distinguish regarding him
between his mother and his daughter-in-law,
so too she — you should not distinguish regarding her
between her mother and her daughter-in-law.
phrases.notes: Her mother gets burning, so her daughter-in-law would also get burning, not stoning.

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say her daughter-in-law gets burning as a final ruling. It only shows that the full comparison clashes with itself, so it cannot be used.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָה הוּא – לֹא חִלַּקְתָּ בּוֹ בֵּין אִמּוֹ לְכַלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After cancelling the objection of step 9, it gives the real refutation of the full comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole full-comparison method (דון מינה ומינה) as a source for her daughter-in-law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Copying his pattern exactly gives her daughter-in-law burning, but the method also demands stoning. It contradicts itself.

steps.title: Even if burning is more severe, this difficulty blocks the derivation
steps.stepSummary: For the view that burning is harsher, the objection of step 8 does not apply. But the problem from step 11 still stops us from learning this law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says burning is more severe, it cannot be derived because of this difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the full-comparison branch. It shows the method fails for both views about which death is harsher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8's refutation, that his side is stricter, only works if סקילה is harsher. Someone who holds שריפה is harsher could avoid that refutation. Even so, the clash from step 11 holds for everyone, so the law still cannot be learned this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning is the more severe death.
It is not derived, meaning we cannot learn the law from here.

steps.whatToRemember: The full comparison (דון מינה ומינה) cannot teach the ban on her daughter-in-law, whichever death you think is harsher.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says burning is more severe,
from this difficulty we do not derive it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׂרֵפָה חֲמוּרָה, מֵהַאי קוּשְׁיָא לָא נְידוּנֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the refutation of step 11 to the view not covered by step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under either view of which death is harsher, the full comparison cannot teach the ban on her daughter-in-law.

steps.title: The other method: learn the ban but keep her side's own punishment
steps.stepSummary: Under דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, we learn that her daughter-in-law is forbidden, but the punishment follows her side's own pattern: burning, like her mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says, 'Learn from it, and then set it in its own place': just as with him his daughter-in-law is forbidden, so too with her, her daughter-in-law is forbidden. And set it in its own place: there it is by stoning, but here it is by burning, as we found with her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tries the second method of comparison. It takes only the prohibition from his side and keeps her side's own punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This method avoids the clash of step 11. We borrow only the idea that a daughter-in-law is forbidden. For the punishment we look at her side, where her mother gets שריפה, so her daughter-in-law gets שריפה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and then set it in its own place. You borrow the basic law but keep the details of the case you are learning about.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says:
Derive from it and set it in its own place,
just as he — his daughter-in-law is forbidden,
so too she — her daughter-in-law is forbidden.
And set it in its own place:
it is there that it is by stoning,
but here — by burning,
as we found with her mother.
phrases.notes: Sleeping with his wife's mother is punished with burning, so her side gets burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְאַתְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the full comparison failed (steps 11–12), it tries the second method that רבא mentioned in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, her daughter-in-law would be forbidden and punished with שריפה, like her mother.

steps.title: If stoning is more severe, his side is stricter and the comparison fails
steps.stepSummary: For the view that סקילה is harsher, even this partial comparison is refuted: his side is stricter, since his mother gets stoning while her mother gets only burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says stoning is more severe, it can be refuted: what about him? His mother is punished with stoning. Will you say the same about her, whose mother is punished with burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second method too, at least for the view that stoning is the harsher death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To learn a law from one case for another, the source case must not be stricter. If סקילה is harsher, his relatives are a stricter group, because his mother gets סקילה while her mother gets שריפה. So we cannot even borrow the basic ban from his side for hers.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning is the more severe death.
There is a way to refute it.
What about this case? It is special because... This is the standard way to show the source case is stricter.

steps.whatToRemember: For the view that סקילה is harsher, neither method can teach the ban on her daughter-in-law from his relatives, because his side is stricter.

phrases.english: According to the one who says stoning is more severe,
it can be refuted:
what about him? His mother is by stoning,
will you say the same about her, whose mother is by burning?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר סְקִילָה חֲמוּרָה, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the partial-comparison method of step 13, using the same reasoning as step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The דון מינה ואוקי באתרה method, but only for the view that סקילה is harsher.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His side is stricter (his mother gets stoning, her mother gets burning), so it cannot be used to teach a law for her side.

steps.title: Another refutation: his side separates daughter from daughter-in-law
steps.stepSummary: On his side, his daughter and daughter-in-law get different deaths. So on her side, her daughter and daughter-in-law should also differ. But the partial comparison gave both of them burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: just as on his side you made a difference between his daughter and his daughter-in-law, so on her side you should make a difference between her daughter and her daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second refutation against the partial comparison (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה) from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave her daughter-in-law burning, like her mother. Her daughter also gets burning. So on her side the daughter and the daughter-in-law would be treated the same. But on his side, his daughter gets burning and his daughter-in-law gets stoning, so the pattern does not match.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
Just as with him, you made a distinction
phrases.notes: "Him" means his side of the family, his own relatives.

phrases.english: between his daughter and his daughter-in-law,
so too with her, you should make a distinction
between her daughter and her daughter-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: מָה הוּא – חִלַּקְתָּ בּוֹ בֵּין בִּתּוֹ לְכַלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second refutation to the one in step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The partial comparison of step 13, on both views
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes her daughter and her daughter-in-law equal, while on his side the two are different

steps.title: Even the view that burning is harsher cannot derive the law
steps.stepSummary: The refutation from step 15 works even for the view that שריפה is harsher, so the law cannot be learned on any view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also for the one who says burning is harsher, we cannot learn it, because of this difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the second method (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה): it cannot teach the ban on her daughter-in-law from his relatives on either view of which death is harsher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refutation in step 14 only worked for the view that סקילה is harsher. The refutation in step 15 does not depend on which death is harsher, so it also defeats the view that שריפה is harsher.

keyTerms.meaning: We cannot derive it, it cannot be learned

steps.whatToRemember: The derivation from his relatives to her relatives fails completely. The refutation in step 15 works no matter which death you think is harsher.

phrases.english: And also according to the one who says
burning is harsher,
because of this difficulty we cannot derive it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר נָמֵי שְׂרֵפָה חֲמוּרָה, מֵהַאי קוּשְׁיָא לָא נְידוּנֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the refutation of step 15 to the other view as well
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The law cannot be derived from his relatives on either view

steps.title: Where do we learn the prohibition of his daughter from a woman he raped?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a man's daughter from a woman he raped is forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: His daughter from a woman he raped: from where do we know she is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks for the source of the prohibition of a man's daughter when her mother is not his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition we have been using is "a woman and her daughter," which is about his wife's daughter. A daughter from a woman he raped is not his wife's daughter, so the גמרא needs another source.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman he raped, who is not his wife

phrases.english: His daughter from a woman he raped,
from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the previous section has ended
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the prohibition and punishment of one's daughter from a woman who is not his wife

steps.title: אביי: a קל וחומר from his granddaughter
steps.stepSummary: אביי reasons that if a man is punished for his daughter's daughter, he is surely punished for his own daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אביי said: it is a קל וחומר. If he is punished for his daughter's daughter, surely he is punished for his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with אביי's teaching, which learns the daughter from the granddaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah clearly forbids a man's daughter's daughter (ויקרא 18:10). His own daughter is a closer relative, so she should surely be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a more serious case

phrases.english: Didn't Abaye say:
it is a קל וחומר:
for his daughter's daughter he is punished,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:10

phrases.english: for his daughter, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the explicit prohibition of his daughter's daughter

steps.title: We do not punish based on a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that בית דין does not give a punishment based only on a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we punish based on a logical argument?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer, using the rule that punishments are not learned from a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר can show that something is forbidden. But the death penalty needs a clearer source in the Torah, so אביי's argument does not seem to be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: From a logical argument, such as a קל וחומר

phrases.english: But do we punish based on a logical argument?
phrases.notes: Here "דין" means a קל וחומר. Punishments need a source in the Torah, not just reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A punishment cannot be given based on a קל וחומר alone

steps.title: It only reveals what the פסוק already includes
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר does not create a new punishment. It only shows that the daughter is already included in the granddaughter's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just revealing the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. His argument is not a real derivation. It only reveals something the פסוק already contains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The granddaughter is forbidden because she comes from his daughter. So the פסוק about the granddaughter already includes the daughter. The קל וחומר just makes that clear, so the punishment really comes from the פסוק itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Revealing the matter; showing what is already there

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say that we do punish based on a קל וחומר. The rule stays in place. It says the daughter was already in the פסוק, and the קל וחומר only points this out.

phrases.english: It is merely revealing the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the argument as a clarification instead of a derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי was creating a punishment through a קל וחומר
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר only shows that the daughter is already included in the granddaughter's פסוק

steps.title: רבא: learned through הנה–הנה and זמה–זמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא, citing רבי יצחק בר אבדימי, gives another source: two גזירה שוה links that tie his own daughter to the burning punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי told me, it is learned from "הנה" and "הנה," and from "זמה" and "זמה."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different source for the daughter from a woman he raped, based on matching words in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "הנה" in the פסוק about his own descendants (ויקרא 18:10) links them to the פסוק about his wife's descendants (ויקרא 18:17). That פסוק says "זמה," and the same word in ויקרא 20:14 links it to the punishment of burning. So his own daughter is forbidden and punished by burning.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from; it comes from a link
"They are"; the word used for the first link
"Lewdness"; the word used for the second link, which brings burning
Learning a law from the same word in two פסוקים

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are two sources for his daughter from a woman he raped: אביי's קל וחומר, which only reveals what the פסוק already includes, and רבא's double גזירה שוה, הנה–הנה and זמה–זמה. The next step brings a third source, from ובת איש כהן.

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי:
phrases.english: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said to me:
it is learned from "they are" and "they are,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:10 and ויקרא 18:17

phrases.english: it is learned from "lewdness" and "lewdness."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17 and ויקרא 20:14, where the punishment of burning is stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, אָמַר לִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי: אָתְיָא ״הֵנָּה״ ״הֵנָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 17, in place of אביי's קל וחומר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His daughter from a woman he raped is forbidden and punished by burning, learned through the double גזירה שוה of הנה–הנה and זמה–זמה

steps.title: A new source from the פסוק of a כהן's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The father of רבי אבין teaches that the Torah had to write ״וּבַת אִישׁ כֹּהֵן״ to teach the case of a man's daughter from a woman he raped.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רבי אבין taught: Since we did not learn about his daughter from a woman he raped, the Torah needed to say 'And the daughter of a כהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third source is given for the daughter from a woman he raped. This one is a ברייתא taught by the father of רבי אבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No פסוק openly mentions this daughter, so the ברייתא finds her inside the פסוק about a כהן's daughter. The words 'את אביה' in that פסוק are read as 'with her father,' and that פסוק ends with burning.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman he raped (not his wife)
And the daughter of a כהן (ויקרא 21:9)
Burning, the death penalty in that פסוק

phrases.english: The father of Rabbi Avin taught:
Since we did not learn
about his daughter from a woman he raped,
the verse needed to say
'And the daughter of a priest.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:9. The פסוק goes on 'את אביה היא מחללת', which is read here as 'with her father.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third source, alongside אביי's קל וחומר and רבא's גזירה שוה, for the question in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter from a woman he raped is learned from ״וּבַת אִישׁ כֹּהֵן״, read as 'with her father,' and the punishment is burning.

steps.title: Maybe only the daughter is burned, as with a כהן's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: with a כהן's daughter only she is burned, not her partner. So maybe here too only the daughter is burned, and the father is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as a כהן's daughter is burned but the man with her is not burned, so too his daughter from a woman he raped is burned, but the man with her is not burned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new source. If we learn from the כהן's daughter, we should copy all her rules, including the rule that her partner is not burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married כהן's daughter who sins is burned, but the man with her gets the regular punishment of any adulterer. Following that pattern here, the father would escape burning, which defeats the point of the source.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, just as... (setting up a comparison to attack)
The man who is with her

phrases.english: If so: just as a priest's daughter —
she is burned
but the man with her is not burned,
so too his daughter from a woman he raped —
she is burned
but the man with her is not burned?
phrases.notes: Here 'the man with her' is her own father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source just given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source from ״וּבַת אִישׁ כֹּהֵן״ in step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is learned from a כהן's daughter, it should copy her rule that only the woman is burned, so the father would not be burned.

steps.title: אביי: the פסוק itself leaves out a case where the father is the sinner
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the words 'her father she profanes' limit the 'partner not burned' rule to a woman who shames her father, not one whose father is the sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says 'It is her father that she profanes.' That means a woman who brings shame on her father. This case is left out, since here her father is the one who profanes her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the objection using the wording of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the partner is not burned fits a daughter who shames her father. When the father himself is the sinner, she is not shaming him; he is shaming her. So that rule does not apply, and the father is burned too.

phrases.english: Abaye said: The verse says
'It is her father that she profanes,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:9

phrases.english: one who profanes her father —
this one is left out, whose father profanes her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23 from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק closely to limit the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every rule of a כהן's daughter carries over, so the father would not be burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'partner not burned' rule applies only to a woman who shames her father, not when the father is the sinner, so he is burned.

steps.title: רבא: the father has no other punishment to fall back on
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with logic: a כהן's daughter's partner falls back to the punishment for a married Israelite woman. Here the father has nothing to fall back on except the law of an unmarried woman, which has no death penalty, and that cannot be.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense there. You took the man out of the law of a כהן's daughter and put him under the law of an Israelite woman. But here, under whose law would you put him? Would you put him under the law of an unmarried woman?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same objection, without needing a special reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a married כהן's daughter, her partner is still punished as an adulterer with a married Israelite woman. With his own daughter, if we take away burning, the only category left is an unmarried woman, who carries no death penalty. Since the Torah surely punishes this, the father must be burned along with her.
steps.whatToRemember: The father with his daughter from a woman he raped is burned. אביי learns it from the words 'her father she profanes'; רבא from logic: without burning, he would have no death penalty at all.

phrases.english: Rava said: It makes sense there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is a married כהן's daughter who sins with another man.

phrases.english: you took him out of the law of a priest's daughter
and placed him under the law of an Israelite woman.
Here, under whose law would you place him?
Would you place him under the law of an unmarried woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, logic-based answer to the קשיא of step 23, instead of אביי's reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning: no fallback punishment exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father should be treated like the partner of a כהן's daughter and not be burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Unlike that partner, the father has no other death penalty to fall back on, so he must be burned too.

steps.title: Where is the prohibition for one's daughter from a raped woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the אזהרה. For אביי and רבא it is easy, but what about אבוה דרבי אבין?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn the prohibition against a man being with his daughter from a woman he raped? For אביי and רבא it is fine: the same source that gives them the punishment also gives them the prohibition. But according to what אבוה דרבי אבין taught, what is the source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has found the punishment, and now asks where the Torah actually forbids this act. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Torah, a punishment needs a matching אזהרה (a warning prohibition). אביי and רבא learned the punishment from sources that also contain a prohibition, so they are covered. But אבוה דרבי אבין learned the punishment from 'ובת איש כהן', which gives only a punishment, so he still needs a source for the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning, meaning the actual Torah prohibition
It makes sense according to... (used to set up a question on the other side)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up עונש and אזהרה. The punishment was already found in earlier steps. Now the גמרא is looking for the prohibition itself.

phrases.english: The prohibition for his daughter from a woman he raped, from where?
Granted, according to אביי and רבא,
from the place where they derive the punishment,
from there they derive the prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לִדְתָנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין, מַאי?
phrases.english: But according to what the father of רבי אבין taught, what is the source?
phrases.notes: He learned the punishment from 'ובת איש כהן' (step 22), a פסוק that does not contain a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing the punishment, the גמרא turns to the matching prohibition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the אזהרה according to אבוה דרבי אבין.

steps.title: רבי אילעא brings the verse 'Do not profane your daughter'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא says the prohibition comes from 'אל תחלל את בתך להזנותה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: The פסוק says, 'Do not profane your daughter by making her act with זנות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא answers the question with a פסוק that warns a man not to bring his daughter to זנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as forbidding a father from being with his own daughter. This gives אבוה דרבי אבין the prohibition (אזהרה) to go with the punishment he learned from ובת איש כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her act with זנות (forbidden relations)

phrases.english: רבי אילעא said:
The verse says,
"Do not profane your daughter by causing her to act licentiously."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אזהרה comes from 'אל תחלל את בתך להזנותה'.

steps.title: That verse is needed for a different lesson
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב objects that the פסוק is already used by a ברייתא to forbid handing a daughter over for זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב, brother of רב אחא בר יעקב, challenged this: Does this פסוק come to teach that? It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not profane your daughter by making her act with זנות.' You might think it means a כהן who marries his daughter to a לוי or a ישראל. So the פסוק says 'to make her act with זנות': it speaks of a profaning that comes through זנות, meaning a man who hands his daughter over not for the sake of marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב attacks רבי אילעא's source. He says the פסוק is already busy teaching something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word 'להזנותה' to show that the פסוק is not about a כהן's daughter marrying a non-כהן. It is about a father giving his daughter to a man for relations without marriage. If the פסוק is used for that, how can רבי אילעא also use it for a father being with his own daughter?

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different lesson)
Not for the sake of marriage

phrases.english: רבי יעקב challenged it,
the brother of רב אחא בר יעקב:
This verse, "Do not profane your daughter by causing her to act licentiously,"
is it for this that it comes?
This is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
"Do not profane your daughter by causing her to act licentiously":
One might think it is about a כהן who marries off his daughter
to a לוי or a ישראל that the verse is speaking?
phrases.notes: Marrying a non-כהן would 'profane' her, since she then loses the right to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "to cause her to act licentiously":
the verse is speaking of a profaning that involves זנות,

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוֹסֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְשֵׁם אִישׁוּת.
phrases.english: about one who hands over his daughter not for the sake of marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given by רבי אילעא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's use of 'אל תחלל את בתך להזנותה' as the prohibition for one's own daughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already used for one lesson (the ברייתא about handing over a daughter for זנות) cannot simply be taken for another.

steps.title: The long word 'תחלל' teaches both lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah could have written 'תחל' but wrote 'תחלל', so we learn two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say 'אל תחל'! Why does it say 'אל תחלל'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אילעא by pointing to an extra letter in the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only taught the ברייתא's lesson, the shorter form 'תחל' would be enough. The Torah used the longer 'תחלל', so it adds a second lesson. That way the ברייתא's lesson and רבי אילעא's prohibition both come from the same פסוק.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "Do not profane (תחל)"!
phrases.notes: 'תחל' is a shorter way to write the same word.

phrases.english: Why does it say "Do not profane (תחלל)"?
Learn two lessons from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יעקב's challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק gives room for a second lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק has room for only one lesson, the ברייתא's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The long form 'תחלל' teaches both the ברייתא's lesson and the prohibition for one's daughter from a raped woman.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אבוה דרבי אבין, the prohibition for one's daughter from a raped woman comes from 'אל תחלל את בתך', and the double letter in 'תחלל' lets the פסוק teach two lessons.

steps.title: What do אביי and רבא learn from this verse?
steps.stepSummary: Since אביי and רבא have another source, the גמרא asks what they do with 'אל תחלל את בתך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי and רבא, what do they do with this פסוק, 'Do not profane your daughter by making her act with זנות'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how אביי and רבא use the extra part of the פסוק, since they don't need it for the prohibition. This sets up רבי מני's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that 'תחלל' teaches two lessons. אביי and רבא already have a source for the prohibition, so the second lesson must teach them something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (How do they use it?)

phrases.english: And אביי and רבא,
this verse, "Do not profane your daughter by causing her to act licentiously,"
what do they do with it?
phrases.notes: He means the second lesson from the long word 'תחלל', since the ברייתא's lesson is accepted by everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא, הַאי ״אַל תְּחַלֵּל אֶת בִּתְּךָ לְהַזְנוֹתָהּ״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the view of אביי and רבא to ask how they use the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lesson אביי and רבא learn from 'אל תחלל'.

steps.title: רבי מני: marrying one's daughter to an old man
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני says the פסוק refers to a man who marries his daughter off to an old man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said: This refers to a man who marries off his daughter to an old man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני answers that for אביי and רבא, the פסוק warns against marrying a daughter to an old man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though this is a real marriage, the פסוק treats it as leading her toward זנות. So the father is blamed for 'profaning' her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the פסוק warns a father not to put his daughter in a match likely to lead her to sin, even inside marriage.

phrases.english: רבי מני said:
This refers to one who marries off his daughter to an old man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי: זֶה הַמַּשִּׂיא אֶת בִּתּוֹ לְזָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For אביי and רבא, the פסוק forbids marrying one's daughter to an old man.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up רבי מני's reading of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר also explains 'אל תחלל את בתך' as marrying a daughter to an old man, while רבי עקיבא explains it as delaying the marriage of a grown daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not profane your daughter by causing her to act immorally.' רבי אליעזר says: This is a man who marries his daughter to an old man. רבי עקיבא says: This is a man who delays marrying off his daughter once she is a grown woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source for what רבי מני just said. It shows that רבי אליעזר learned the same idea from this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31, רבי מני said the פסוק is about marrying a daughter to an old man. The ברייתא shows this is already the view of רבי אליעזר. רבי עקיבא reads the same פסוק differently: it is about a father who delays his grown daughter's marriage. Either way, the father's choice may push her toward זנות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
One who delays or holds back
A girl who has reached full adulthood

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מני's view matches רבי אליעזר in the ברייתא, not רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא gives a different case: delaying the marriage of a grown daughter.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Do not profane your daughter by causing her to act immorally."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:29

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
This is one who marries off his daughter to an old man.
רבי עקיבא says:
This is one who delays the marriage of his daughter who is a grown woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ברייתא source for רבי מני's reading in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מני's claim that 'אל תחלל את בתך' refers to marrying a daughter to an old man.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר gives the same reading, and רבי עקיבא gives the case of delaying a grown daughter's marriage.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא lists who counts as the truly 'poor' in ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא quotes רבי עקיבא: the only 'poor' person in ישראל is a רשע ערום and a father who delays the marriage of his grown daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי עקיבא: You have no poor person in ישראל except a sneaky wicked person, and one who delays the marriage of his grown daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related saying of רבי עקיבא. He names two kinds of people who fall into the category of 'עני'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to רבי עקיבא's view in the ברייתא, where delaying a grown daughter's marriage was the meaning of the פסוק. Here he lists two kinds of people: a רשע ערום, and the father who delays his daughter's marriage. Listing them as two separate items sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A sneaky, cunning wicked person who hides his true nature

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי עקיבא:
You have no poor person among the Jewish people
except a sneaky wicked person,
and one who delays the marriage of his grown daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching of רבי עקיבא about the father who delays a grown daughter's marriage, from the case in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two kinds of people are called 'poor' in ישראל: a רשע ערום, and a father who delays marrying off his grown daughter.

steps.title: Isn't the delaying father himself a sneaky wicked person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא lists the delaying father separately, since he seems to be a רשע ערום himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that one who delays the marriage of his grown daughter is not a sneaky wicked person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's list. Why name the delaying father as a separate item, if he already fits under רשע ערום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying lists two items: a רשע ערום, and the delaying father. The גמרא points out that the delaying father seems to be a clear example of a רשע ערום, so the second item looks unneeded. An answer must explain who the 'רשע ערום' in the first item is.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: Is that to say that one who delays the marriage of his grown daughter
is not a sneaky wicked person?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ הַמַּשְׁהֶא בִּתּוֹ בּוֹגֶרֶת לָאו רָשָׁע עָרוּם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבי עקיבא's list in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's list of two separate items: רשע ערום and the delaying father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The delaying father is himself a רשע ערום, so listing him separately seems unneeded.

steps.title: אביי begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to answer the question about רבי עקיבא's list. His actual answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move: אביי is about to answer the question from step 34. Only the opening words of his answer appear here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי will explain the list so that the two items do not overlap. His words continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי said (the opening of his answer)

phrases.english: אביי said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the challenge in step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pending: the content of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The delaying father seems to be counted twice in רבי עקיבא's list.
steps.terutzMaskana: To be given by אביי on the next amud.
